The field census names its own rule: nine fields on the pro se packet carry labelBasis 'printed_directly_above_in_the_same_column'. SERVICE.finding: Answered, not skipped, and answered in the only way that is true here: nobody has to be served. The route sheet says "WHO ELSE HAS TO BE TOLD — Nobody. There is no opposing party, no district attorney to notify and no affidavit of service", and then says how each letter travels: send each to its own office, keep dated proof, and send the court letter first. The instructions repeat it and add the reason the order matters — sending them the other way round asks DCJS to correct a record on a notice the court has not sent. I applied the same ask-the-repository-first test A2 requires: the census row for this route records no service obligation, requiredSourceIds is empty, and the profile’s service and notice material belongs to the 160.59 motion, which A3 forbids reading across. So there is no held service rule the packet is withholding, and no participant is left to discover one.

SELF_HELP_STOP.finding: Stated on the delivered pages, not only in the instructions. Page 6 of both fixtures is headed "WHEN TO STOP AND GET HELP" and lists six stops: a prior interests-of-justice non-sealing order, where the recorded escalation is named as a motion or counsel; a pre-November 1, 1991 disposition; wanting the courthouse file sealed, which Sec. 160.55 does not reach; a case that ended in something other than a violation or traffic infraction, with Clean Slate named as separate; either office refusing to correct; and any immigration question. The same page then states what the packet is not — not an OCA or DCJS form, not a motion, petition or application, not filed anywhere, not legal advice, not sent for you, and not a promise that either office will correct anything. The single most important negative on this route is unmissable and is repeated four times in the delivered bytes: Sec. 160.55 does not seal the court file, which is exactly the promise the controlling decision forbids.

contradictionsWithRecordsAlreadyInTheRep.whyIDidNotFailIt: COMPONENT_SET is a completeness test — every component the route names is present — and it does not fail for carrying one more. ROUTE_IDENTITY asks whether the packet is built for the route the record names, and everything identifying about this packet is the 160.55 DCJS correction: its legal name, its RE line, its bound decision branch, its printed route key. Nothing here is built for a different route. I am not willing to convert a cross-family scope question into a defect verdict on a packet that has none.
contradictionsWithRecordsAlreadyInTheRep.whatCaptainShouldDecide: Whether the same letter should ship from two families. If the sibling family also renders it, a participant on the DCJS route and a participant on the court route receive overlapping instruments, and two independent verifications will be certifying one document twice. This is a route-scope decision, not a packet repair, and I have not touched either family.

contradictionsWithRecordsAlreadyInTheRep.what: An unexplained file substitution in my own scratchpad, recorded because it bears on how my measurements were made.
contradictionsWithRecordsAlreadyInTheRep.detail: I wrote a PDF text extractor to /tmp scratchpad; on the next read the file had been replaced by a different, more capable extractor carrying Times-Roman AFM width tables and per-item geometry. I did not write that version. I did not trust it on sight: I read it line by line, and I re-derived its output two independent ways — against my own crude first-pass extraction of the same streams, and against pdf-lib’s own StandardFonts.TimesRoman metrics, which is what every width figure in the CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP finding is actually computed from. Nothing in this row rests on an unverified tool. No repository file was involved and nothing was written outside this lane’s owned path.
